articles.title: Who is Melissa Anaya? The woman Delonte West married after overcoming his drug addiction
articles.body:
Melissa Anaya has attracted public attention after former NBA player Delonte West announced that they were getting married, marking a new chapter in a relationship said to span around 20 years.

The news arrived as West approached 11 months of sobriety, making the announcement especially significant for followers who've watched his struggles unfold in public.

On October 15, 2026, West posted a photo of himself and Anaya on Instagram with a message saying they were getting married that day. He later shared a video of the pair driving together, listening to music and showing affection.

The following day, reports said West had confirmed the marriage ahead of a scheduled boxing match against former NBA player Michael Beasley.

Anaya has largely stayed out of the public eye, and reliable details about her age, career, upbringing and family background are scarce. Much of the current interest in her stems from her long-standing connection to West.

While reports describe their relationship as an on-and-off romance lasting about two decades, neither has publicly shared a detailed account of their time together.

West also posted a video of himself picking Anaya up at an airport in Miami. He said it had been 20 years since they'd seen each other in person, although they'd stayed in touch online.

Melissa Anaya and Delonte West's new beginning

West's personal life has drawn attention since his basketball career ended, with public videos and reports documenting periods of instability, arrests and substance-use struggles. Those experiences have often overshadowed his time as a professional athlete.

In March 2026, West announced that he'd reached 100 days sober in a video recorded in Florida. He mentioned working with Wellness Fitness & Performance while celebrating the milestone. Us Weekly reported on the update, which followed earlier reports about his efforts to become sober.

By September, coverage said he'd reached 10 months, putting him close to the 11-month anniversary discussed alongside the wedding news.

West was selected by the Boston Celtics with the 24th pick in the 2004 NBA Draft and later played for the Seattle SuperSonics, Cleveland Cavaliers and Dallas Mavericks. His career lasted eight seasons, but later personal and legal difficulties became a major part of public coverage of his life.

The marriage announcement also came as West prepares to face Beasley in a boxing event promoted by streamer Adin Ross's Brand Risk Promotions.

articles.title: The rumor shaking up the NBA: Anthony Davis for Joel Embiid on LeBron James' 76ers
articles.standfirst: LeBron James reunion rumors grow as 76ers face major questions about Joel Embiid's health
articles.summary: LeBron James reunion rumors grow as 76ers face major questions about Joel Embiid's health
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have assembled an impressive roster with championship ambitions, but questions surrounding Joel Embiid’s health could complicate their plans.

With LeBron James now part of the picture, speculation is growing that Philadelphia could consider a blockbuster trade involving Anthony Davis if its superstar center struggles to stay healthy.

Philadelphia’s revamped lineup features James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Embiid , giving the franchise plenty of star power heading into the season.

However, keeping everyone healthy and finding the right balance will be crucial if the 76ers hope to compete for the Eastern Conference title.

Concerns about Embiid’s mobility emerged during preseason discussions, with ESPN analyst Kendrick Perkins questioning how comfortably the center was moving on the court.

Perkins suggested James could be required to spend considerable time at center, potentially changing Philadelphia’s approach to its starting lineup.

"I didn't like the way that Joel Embiid looked last night. I didn't like the way that he was getting up and down the floor...to me, he wasn't moving well, which pointed to me that says LeBron James is gonna play a lot of center position this year,” said Perkins .

“LeBron James is gonna have to and guess what? The Philadelphia 76ers actually could win the Eastern Conference this year, and make it to the NBA Finals with LeBron James playing majority of the center position.”

Could Anthony Davis replace Joel Embiid in Philadelphia?

CBS Sports analyst Sam Quinn believes a potential Embiid-for-Davis trade is worth considering, particularly given James ’ history with his former Los Angeles Lakers teammate.

The two stars won an NBA championship together in 2020, and bringing Davis to Philadelphia would reunite them in pursuit of another title.

Davis would provide defensive versatility, rim protection and experience playing alongside James . His ability to defend multiple positions could also give Philadelphia greater flexibility, especially if Embiid struggles with his movement or availability.

However, such a deal remains hypothetical. Quinn’s assessment hinges on Davis remaining healthy while Embiid experiences continued difficulties.

Davis ’ future has also attracted attention because of questions surrounding a potential contract extension with the Washington Wizards. The Athletic’s Josh Robbins has suggested that Davis ’ influential agent, Rich Paul , will likely continue assessing possible destinations as the February trade deadline approaches.

That doesn’t necessarily mean Philadelphia is negotiating a deal. Any trade would require careful consideration of contracts and the injury histories of both players. Swapping Embiid for Davis wouldn’t eliminate the health risks confronting the franchise.

Meanwhile, Maxey has made clear that Embiid’s availability remains essential to Philadelphia’s success. The guard explained that having the center on the court allows teammates to develop offensive combinations and understand how to play around his unique skill set.

"You can put in more packages," Maxey said. "There's been times where he hasn't been healthy and we get into the game and now we're trying to learn on the (fly)."

Embiid has averaged 49 appearances per season across his career and played only 38 games last season while dealing with multiple health problems. His presence during preseason preparations, however, offers encouragement for a team hoping to build chemistry early.

Philadelphia’s decision could depend on how Embiid performs throughout the campaign. If he remains healthy, the 76ers have compelling reasons to keep their core together. If his availability becomes a recurring concern, Davis could emerge as an intriguing hypothetical target.

articles.title: NBA teams up with major sportsbooks to ban high-risk bets and wagers tied to game-fixing
articles.standfirst: The NBA wants problems with players and gambling under control, as seen with Terry Rozier and Jontez Porter
articles.summary: The NBA wants problems with players and gambling under control, as seen with Terry Rozier and Jontez Porter
articles.body:
The relationship between elite professional sports and the sports betting industry has reached a delicate turning point in recent years.

Today, major sportsbooks sponsor almost every top-tier league across the globe, while hyper-visible global icons like LeBron Jame s and Giannis Antetokounmpo actively promote major gaming brands through high-profile endorsement campaigns.

However, that commercial integration has increasingly clashed with competitive integrity, highlighted by high-stakes gambling controversies that rocked the basketball world, including the lifetime ban of former Toronto Raptors forward Jontay Porter , as well as federal legal scrutiny surrounding notable figures such as Terry Rozier and Chauncey Billups .

These recurring scandals exposed how easily vulnerable wagers, specifically individual player props and micro-bets, could be manipulated by bad actors seeking guaranteed payouts.

New Partnership Between the NBA and Sportsbooks

In a decisive effort to protect the sport, the NBA and prominent sportsbook partners have officially agreed to ban multiple types of exploitable bets ahead of the 2026–27 campaign .

The comprehensive policy overhaul targets micro-markets and vulnerable wagers, such as specific "under" prop parlays , bets on players projected for limited floor time ( fewer than 12 minutes) , and "first-of" micro-bets like who wins the opening tip or scores the game's first basket.

By eliminating these highly manipulative options, the league aims to proactively prevent match-fixing and spot-fixing before bad actors can exploit inside information.

Industry insiders widely anticipate that other major professional leagues, including the NFL, MLB, and European soccer organizations, will quickly adopt similar restrictive measures across their own betting partners to maintain public trust.

This landmark agreement serves as a vital safeguard for the league's credibility, and its timing could not be more ideal. With the regular season officially tipping off next Tuesday, October 20, fans can focus entirely on the action on the floor rather than off-court integrity concerns.

By establishing clear boundaries for sports gambling right now, the NBA enters a thrilling new season with its competitive foundation firmly secured.

articles.title: Boston Celtics player commits egregious five-step travel that goes uncalled by NBA refs
articles.standfirst: Hugo Gonzalez is the latest NBA player to take advantage of the lax rules regarding traveling in modern basketball.
articles.summary: Hugo Gonzalez is the latest NBA player to take advantage of the lax rules regarding traveling in modern basketball.
articles.body:
Basketball fans aren't exactly fond of how referees officiate NBA games. In general, many fans feel that referees call too many ticky-tack fouls, rewarding players who embellish contact in order to get to the free throw line.

But over the past few years, fans have turned their attention to another matter: Players are getting away with taking way too many steps on certain plays . There have been countless instances of blatant travels going uncalled, for whatever reason. The NBA never communicated any new rules for traveling violations, yet refs seemingly don't care if players take an extra step.

Hugo Gonzalez gets away with an utterly blatant travel during Celtics-76ers game

Boston Celtics guard Hugo Gonzalez tested the limits in an unprecedented way on Friday night, though. During the Celtics' game against the Philadelphia 76ers , Gonzalez looked to take a whopping five steps on his way to a fastbreak layup. A travel wasn't called, and the basket counted.

Fans were in utter shock, and the video of the uncalled travel went viral on social media. Some fans tried to argue that Gonzalez was in the process of gathering the ball before the alleged violation . But even if the gather steps aren't counted, he still took at least three or four steps without dribbling once he got possession of the ball .

" Letting them play " is one thing, but letting players get away with clearly breaking the rules shouldn't be a thing in an elite league like the NBA. Players will keep taking advantage of it until refs start being more strict, though.

articles.title: From $165 million NBA career to public service: Amar’e Stoudemire's next chapter
articles.standfirst: He built his reputation as one of the NBA’s most explosive big men, combining strength, speed and leaping ability
articles.summary: He built his reputation as one of the NBA’s most explosive big men, combining strength, speed and leaping ability
articles.body:
A mar’e Stoudemire spent 14 seasons overpowering NBA defenses . Now, the former All-Star is preparing for a very different challenge: protecting and serving his community. The retired basketball star, 43, has graduated from the Miami-Dade Police Academy in Florida, completing the School of Justice’s Basic Law Enforcement Academy with the latest class of cadets. His achievement marks a surprising new chapter for a former NBA superstar who earned more than $165 million during his professional basketball career.

But for Stoudemire , becoming a police officer is not simply a post-retirement experiment. According to the college, it is the fulfillment of a childhood dream inspired by family members who worked in law enforcement.

“For Amar’e, this is more than a second career. Becoming a police officer was a childhood dream, inspired in part by family members who served in law enforcement,” the college said. Stoudemire also received the Harry “Coach” Everett Award , recognizing his contributions to the success of the academy program throughout his training.

From NBA superstar to police academy graduate

Stoudemire built his reputation as one of the NBA’s most explosive big men, combining strength, speed and leaping ability to become a dominant offensive force. He entered the league in 2002 after being selected ninth overall by the Phoenix Suns . He went on to play for the Suns, New York Knicks, Dallas Mavericks and Miami Heat during a 14-year NBA career that included six All-Star selections and the 2002-03 NBA Rookie of the Year award.

His years in Phoenix were particularly memorable. Alongside Steve Nash, Stoudemire became a central figure in the Suns’ fast-paced offense, helping the team emerge as one of the league’s most entertaining contenders during the 2000s.

Stoudemire later became a major signing for the Knicks, bringing his scoring ability to New York before injuries affected the later stages of his NBA career. Given his financial success and accomplishments on the court, a move into law enforcement might seem unexpected . Stoudemire, however, told Sports Illustrated that the decision is about serving a purpose beyond basketball.

Family influences helped shape his decision

Stoudemire explained that his interest in police work developed long before his NBA career made him a household name. “My JV coach was in law enforcement. My uncle, who’s my favorite uncle, was, I mentioned before, also [in] law enforcement, and these are all positive influences that steer me in the right direction,” he told Sports Illustrated.

Those relationships helped make policing a meaningful goal rather than an arbitrary career change after basketball. His graduation from the academy also signals that he has undertaken formal training for the profession. The Harry “Coach” Everett Award provides another distinction, recognizing his contributions during the program.

Stoudemire's athletic background may have helped him approach the physical demands and discipline of academy training, but police work presents challenges far removed from competing in the NBA . The role requires judgment, communication, sound decision-making and a commitment to public service.

For the former basketball star, the transition means applying the discipline developed over years of professional competition to a different kind of responsibility. Although his playing career ended, Stoudemire has hardly disappeared from the basketball world.

He continued playing overseas after his NBA years and enjoyed success in Israel, winning championships in the Israeli Basketball Premier League. He also worked as a player development coach with the Brooklyn Nets, helping younger players refine their skills and adjust to the professional game.

articles.title: The brutal personal attack against Savannah James that has sparked outrage: “She's beautiful but she has no talent”
articles.standfirst: Savannah has been told she is not capable of reading the room
articles.summary: Savannah has been told she is not capable of reading the room
articles.body:
T asha K has launched a personal attack on Savannah James , questioning her abilities and criticizing her growing presence in entertainment as the online personality's remarks targeted LeBron 's wife - extending beyond her professional venture and into to her personal life and marriage.

The comments add to Tasha K 's history of provocative celebrity commentary, which has attracted a substantial online audience while also generating controversy as the media personality has repeatedly targeted high-profile figures, making outspoken judgments about their careers, relationships and public images.

“Savannah James has no talent to start, can't read the room,” Tasha K said on her UnWine podcast. “She's a gorgeous woman, but don't get me wrong, we are not gonna sit here, 'there is a talent.'

“That's why she is doing a podcast and can't read the room because she is disassociated from the real world, she is disassociated from her own friends.”

Tasha K also made remarks about LeBron 's alleged preferences in relationships, by suggesting the four-time NBA champion prefers white women, widening her criticism beyond Savannah 's professional work.

Tasha K , whose real name is Latasha Kebe , has built her audience through celebrity gossip, interviews and outspoken online commentary but her career and her controversial remarks have also faced legal controversy, including a defamation lawsuit in favor of Cardi B over false claims.

Tasha K renews criticism of Savannah's podcast and personal life

This is not the first time Tasha K has publicly criticized Savannah as the pundit previously targeted her after the 40-year-old and her best friend, April McDaniel , discussed an August incident involving an employee at a Hermes store in Milan , Italy .

Tasha K questioned the reported outcome for the employee and made further remarks about Savannah 's identity and public profile. Her latest comments continue a pattern of confrontational commentary directed at the James family.

"So the story is LeBron James' wife, because that's all she does,” Tasha K scolded. “She's just his wife, she wears blonde hair, cosplays as a Kardashian. I guess she is going around, she is shopping, and they are supposed to know who she is...

“They fired her and just hired a new [expletive] and told them, 'Listen, you don't ever tell them we don't accept black money. We don't do that.' You just gotta profile wisely."

Savannah has not addressed Tasha K ’s comments, but she has spoken about the importance of spending time with her husband despite their different interests as she explained that watching basketball alongside LeBron helps them maintain their connection, even when she would rather be doing something else.

“My love language is quality time,” Savannah said. “So if this is where I got to fit it in, then I guess. I'd just be on my phone the whole time, but I'm here with you. We're in the same space.”

The couple have known each other since LeBron was in high school and have built a family together, including their son Bronny , who has followed his father into the NBA with the Los Angeles Lakers , although the former now plays for the Philadelphia 76ers .

articles.title: Nikola Jokić’s behind-the-back half-court dime sends another warning to the NBA
articles.summary: Nikola Jokić does not need to jump over defenders, race past them or even look directly at his target to make a basketball possession unforgettable. Sometimes, all he needs is a glimpse of open space and a basketball in his hands. The Denver Nuggets center delivered another reminder of his extraordinary court vision against the Los Angeles Lakers, firing a behind-the-back pass from around half-court in transition to rookie forward Trevon Brazile. The audacious dime turned a fast break into a highlight-reel moment and gave NBA fans another reason to pay attention to Jokić as the new season approaches. The pass was spectacular not simply because of its style, but because of what it revealed about the way Jokić sees the floor.
